Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for the SIG intake. Quick answers up front: we can complete the SIG (see timeline below), we have a DPA template and SCC approach we provide to EU customers, and HIPAA/BAA is feasible but depends on deployment mode and some minimal operational commitments.

Plan / timeline:
- By EOD Friday (2026-03-06): we will upload a completed SIG spreadsheet covering our hosted and private deployment controls.
- By Wednesday (2026-03-11): legal team can share a drafted BAA + DPA redlines for your counsel to review.

Key notes for your security team:
- Hosted Redwood: we encrypt data at rest and in transit, maintain SOC 2 Type II controls (summary attached), and provide tenant isolation + customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private offerings.
- Private/VPC or On‑Prem: typical workflow for PHI is to run Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS and on‑prem networking — this is the path we recommend for PHI where a signed BAA is required.

CC'ing Neha (security/compliance) and Diego (platform infra) to validate the SIG responses and confirm any technical artifacts we should attach (network diagrams, SOC2 summary, etc.).

Regards,

Thanks Priyom — a few internal clarifications for how we'll complete the SIG and position HIPAA: 

- SIG: I'll take point on the SIG spreadsheet. I'll indicate controls mapped to our SOC 2 controls and supply evidence stubs (policy links + SOC2 summary). For items that vary by deployment (Hosted vs Private), we'll provide two columns and recommend Private for PHI.

- BAA feasibility: we will agree to a BAA for customers that run in our Private or Dedicated environments where customer-managed keys and network isolation are in place. For Hosted (shared tenancy), we typically do not sign BAAs unless we have a contract for Dedicated capacity and specific architecture/commitments.

- SCCs & DPA: we have an updated DPA template that includes SCCs references and standard transfer mechanisms. We will flag the specific data flow sections that relate to cross-border patient referral scenarios.

- Evidence to attach to MedCare: SOC2 summary (latest), encryption key management note, logging/audit retention matrix, and a high-level architecture diagram for Private deployment. Diego — can you produce the architecture + logging retention snippet?

I'll aim to upload the SIG and attach the four artifacts by EOD 2026-03-06.

Neha Kapoor
Head of InfoSec & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Copying the artifacts we can provide:

- onprem-architecture-hipaa-note.pdf: shows recommended Private deployment topology for PHI (customer VPC, private subnet inference nodes, customer KMS/HSM).
- logging-retention.txt (included inside the PDF): we retain request & audit logs for 365 days by default; for Dedicated/Private customers we can configure longer retention via contract. Logs include user/operator actions and model request hashes; full request bodies are treated per DPA clauses.
- encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest; for Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys.

I'll attach the architecture PDF and a short logging matrix to the SIG package.

—Diego
